lesson.face_expressions.title: Face & Expressions
lesson.face_expressions.summary: Build a simple face with clear landmarks, then change the features to create an expression that feels like yours.
lesson.face_expressions.step.head: Start with the overall head shape. Compare its height and width before worrying about features.
lesson.face_expressions.help.head: Use the center guide to check balance. The two sides do not need to be perfectly identical.
lesson.face_expressions.complete.head: The main head construction is in place.
lesson.face_expressions.step.eyes: Place the eyes and brows around the same horizontal area. Use symmetry as a guide, not a score.
lesson.face_expressions.help.eyes: Compare each eye's distance from the center and the space between the brows. Small differences can add character.
lesson.face_expressions.complete.eyes: Your main eye and brow landmarks are established.
lesson.face_expressions.step.features: Add the nose and mouth by comparing their position to the eyes and center of the face.
lesson.face_expressions.help.features: Look at the vertical spacing: eyes first, then nose, then mouth. Adjust the relationship rather than chasing perfect lines.
lesson.face_expressions.complete.feature: The face now has its main landmarks.
lesson.face_expressions.step.expression: Now change the brows, eyes or mouth to choose a feeling. Calm, curious, excited, worried or something completely invented all work.
lesson.face_expressions.help.expression: Try changing one feature at a time and notice how the feeling shifts. There is no reference expression you need to match.
lesson.face_expressions.complete.drawing: You built the face structure and made the expression your own.
